newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador says needs private funds for energy sector.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador says needs private funds for energy sector.

text.p: Ecuador's government does not have the funds to end the country's energy deficit and critically needs private investment to improve energy supplies, a top official said Thursday.

Donald Castillo, manager of electricity company Instituto Ecuatoriano de Electrificacion (INECEL), speaking in a television interview, said at the beginning of 1996 that the energy deficit was greater than 400 megawatts.
Ecuador's Congress approved INECEL's selloff Thursday.

Castillo said the efficient management of electricity generators had allowed electricity rationing to be eliminated in February "even though we have had months and days when the supplies have been as low as 50 cubic metres per second while the necessary minimum is 120 cubic metres per second."
Last week electricity works at various electricity installations were speeded up.
"Private capital has to enter the industry because the state does not have the resources necessary to expand the system," said Castillo.
Ecuador depends almost exclusively on the Paute power station, which generates 70 percent of the country's energy.
The INECEL head predicted $250 million will have to be invested yearly in the years to come.
Ecuador suffered a severe energy crisis in 1995, with electricity rationing for up to eight hours daily.
